descricao_original: Anaphase begins as chiasmata break, allowing homologous chromosomes to separate. Unlike mitosis, sister chromatids remain attached by cohesive proteins at their centromeres, and their kinetochores function together. Anaphase ends with the segregation of one duplicated chromosome of each homologous pair to each spindle pole.
